call.method: vectorised bisection on _common.bs_normalized_price over every evaluated row (no subsampling)
call.source: inverted from mid/K stored in the HDF5; OptionMetrics' per-contract impl_volatility is not retained there and the 8.6 GB optionPrice_2015_2025.csv was NOT read

observed_iv.preferred: stored OptionMetrics impl_volatility (falling back to the inversion where it is missing)
observed_iv.note: the inversion is NaN wherever vega is uninformative (deep wings) or the quote violates the no-arbitrage band, so a large p95 there is expected and is a property of those rows, not of either source

put.method: vectorised bisection on _common.bs_normalized_price over every evaluated row (no subsampling)
put.source: inverted from mid/K stored in the HDF5; OptionMetrics' per-contract impl_volatility is not retained there and the 8.6 GB optionPrice_2015_2025.csv was NOT read

observed_iv.preferred: stored OptionMetrics impl_volatility (falling back to the inversion where it is missing)

strata.T_eq_0: T == 0 (expiry-day contracts). BS is intrinsic here for ANY sigma, so every baseline scores identically in this stratum by construction.
strata.T_gt_0_le_1d: 0 < T <= 1/365. EMPTY in this dataset: T = days_to_expiry/365 is quantised, and the float32-stored 1-day value (0.00273973) is just ABOVE 1/365 (0.00273972602...), so 1-day contracts fall in T_gt_1d. This is the same comparison _common.compute_metrics makes, so the model's headline R2(log, T>1/365) also includes the 1-day contracts.
strata.T_gt_1d: T > 1/365 -- the headline log-metric domain (see CLAUDE.md).
strata.T_eq_1d: extra, non-exclusive: round(T*365) == 1, i.e. the 1-day contracts that T_gt_0_le_1d would have held if T were exact.

labels.branch: the neural input branch this baseline is a legitimate comparator for (built from the same information that branch sees); null = none, in which case the baseline is a context-free reference point and says nothing about any branch
labels.input_kind: what the baseline's own input actually is: 'branch-comparable' | 'scalar market observable (not a branch input)' | 'lagged market observable (not a branch input)' | 'context-free reference (no market input)'
labels.why: the scalar-VIX baselines were previously tagged branch='vix_history', which invites the invalid inference that the VIX-history branch beats the vol-surface branch. Different input, different information content.

meta.vix_anti_inference: ANTI-INFERENCE: this is a contemporaneous scalar VIX benchmark (one index close per date) and NOT the model's `vix_history` branch (a 21x4 OHLC tensor, close-normalised so the absolute VIX level is destroyed), so it cannot be used to rank the neural input branches against each other.
meta.pricer: analysis/_common.bs_normalized_price, float64, log(clip(price, 1e-8)) exactly as in training
